paper_title: deepfakebench: a comprehensive benchmark of deepfake detection
descriptions: DeepfakeBench is a comprehensive benchmark framework for deepfake detection intended to provide a standardized, unified platform for fair comparison across detectors. It includes a unified data management/data preprocessing pipeline (frame extraction, face cropping, alignment, optional mask and landmark generation, and a JSON-based arrangement for consistent train/test/validation splits), a modular training framework supporting 15 detector methods across naive, spatial, and frequency categories, and an evaluation/analysis module providing standardized metrics and visualization tools. The paper does not define a single “labeled attribute” dataset; rather, it curates and organizes multiple existing deepfake video/image datasets into a uniform format and enriches some of them with aligned forgery masks. The envisioned ML task is frame-level deepfake detection (fake vs real), evaluated using metrics such as frame-level AUC/AP/EER and related visual analyses.

descriptions: ERATO is a large-scale dataset created to support the Pairwise Emotional Relationship Recognition (PERR) task, which classifies the emotional relationship between two interactive characters in a video clip. paper_title: riganyface: scaling neural facial mesh auto-rigging with unlabeled data

paper_title: dcface: synthetic face generation with dual condition diffusion model

descriptions: The paper introduces DCFace, a two-stage synthetic face generation scheme meant to produce training data for face recognition (FR) that improves subject label consistency while matching real-data style diversity. paper_title: wilddeepfake: a challenging real-world dataset for deepfake detection
descriptions: WildDeepfake is introduced to support deepfake detectors against real-world deepfakes by providing a dataset collected completely from the internet (both real and deepfake videos are sourced from the web). The dataset is organized as face sequences extracted from 707 deepfake videos, yielding 7,314 face sequences and 1,180,099 face images annotated into real and fake categories (unknown and conflicting labels are discarded). Collection involves keyword-based retrieval of videos with "deepfake", filtering out videos created with traditional (non-deepfake) face manipulations, and manual verification that each deepfake video has a real counterpart; frames are processed with face detection, MobileNetV2 feature extraction, and dlib landmark-based alignment, followed by labeling by three trained human annotators. The envisioned ML task is deepfake detection, evaluated in the paper at both image-level (single face) and sequence-level (face sequence) using binary classification networks.

paper_title: mafw: a large-scale, multi-modal, compound affective database for dynamic facial expression recognition in the wild
descriptions: MAFW is proposed as a large-scale, multi-modal, compound affective database for dynamic facial expression recognition in the wild. It contains 298 videos (over 30 hours) sourced from YouTube, capturing spontaneous reactions across varied conditions including different ethnicities, head poses, illumination conditions, and occlusions. The dataset provides per-frame continuous annotations of valence and arousal in the range [-1, +1], generated via an online time-continuous joystick annotation procedure and then post-processed by multi-stage verification and selection; final labels are the mean of annotations selected by two additional experts. The intended ML tasks are dimensional emotion prediction (regression of valence and arousal over time) and related evaluation under the Aff-Wild Challenge; it can also be used for deriving priors for other emotion recognition settings.

paper_title: webface260m: a benchmark unveiling the power of million-scale deep face recognition
descriptions: WebFace42M (Cleaned) is the cleaned training subset derived from WebFace260M using an automatic cleaning pipeline called Cleaning Automatically by Self-Training (CAST). It contains 2M identities and 42M faces, where the paper describes iterative intra-class and inter-class cleaning based on embeddings from teacher/student ResNet-100 + ArcFace models, followed by duplicate removal and removal of overlaps with popular benchmarks and the paper’s test set. Beyond identity/face data, WebFace42M provides 7 face attribute annotations (pose, age, race, gender, hat, glass, and mask), and the paper reports distribution statistics for pose, age, and race. The intended ML task is training deep face recognition systems for large-scale face matching/verification, evaluated via time-constrained FRUITS protocols and comparison benchmarks (e.g., IJB-C, NIST-FRVT).

paper_title: general facial representation learning in a visual-linguistic manner
descriptions: LAION-FACE is a curated subdataset derived from the large openly available image-text pair dataset LAION. The authors filter LAION images using the RetinaFace face detector and randomly sample 20 million image-text pairs where the face detection score exceeds 0.9. Each dataset item is an image (containing a face region) paired with a natural-language web text caption. The dataset is intended to support weakly-supervised visual-linguistic pretraining for general facial representation learning using image-text contrastive learning and masked image modeling, with the learned representations transferred to downstream face analysis tasks.

descriptions: The CMU-MOSEI dataset is introduced as the largest multimodal dataset for sentiment analysis and emotion recognition. It contains annotated video segments/utterances with synchronized language (manual transcription), visual information (facial expressions/landmarks), and acoustic information (paralinguistic/prosody features). Sentiment is labeled on a Likert scale [-3,3], and Ekman emotions {happiness, sadness, anger, fear, disgust, surprise} are labeled for presence on a [0,3] Likert scale; annotations are produced by three crowdsourced Amazon Mechanical Turk judges with a short training video and are limited to master workers with >98% approval rate. The envisioned ML tasks are supervised sentiment regression/classification and emotion recognition using multimodal fusion models.

paper_title: guard me if you know me: protecting specific face-identity from deepfakes
descriptions: VIPBench is an identity-centric benchmark introduced to evaluate personalized, identity-aware deepfake detection. The benchmark focuses on scenarios where prior knowledge of a target individual (“VIP”) is available, unlike conventional deepfake benchmarks that treat faces generically. VIPBench is constructed from 22 target identities and includes both real images and forged samples produced by 14 state-of-the-art face manipulation methods (7 face-swapping and 7 entire-face synthesis). The benchmark is intended to assess detection performance (and supports identity-aware evaluation through fine-grained annotations), with a dedicated user-specific evaluation split (VIPEval) and accompanying training/evaluation components described in the paper.

paper_title: webface260m: a benchmark unveiling the power of million-scale deep face recognition
descriptions: WebFace260M is a million-scale face recognition training benchmark built to bridge the data gap between academia and industry. It is constructed by collecting a celebrity name list (about 4M) and downloading 260M faces from the Internet, followed by face detection and alignment using five landmarks predicted by RetinaFace. The dataset is then used as the noisy source for subsequent automatic cleaning (CAST) to produce the cleaned WebFace42M; WebFace260M itself is presented as the initial, noisy collection and is not described as having per-image identity-attribute labels. The envisioned ML task is large-scale deep face recognition training, including verification/matching under later evaluation protocols (FRUITS) described in the paper.

paper_title: the deepfake detection challenge dataset
descriptions: The DFDC dataset was constructed to enable training of deepfake/face-swap detection models and to support the DeepFake Detection Challenge (DFDC) Kaggle competition. It contains short (10-second) face-swap videos produced using multiple face-swapping methods (Deepfake/GAN-based and non-learned methods), plus non-Deepfaked/organic clips, along with audio-swapped clips included for breadth of manipulation. The paper describes source collection by commissioning videos of paid actors who agreed to have their faces manipulated, and it does not present additional per-actor demographic attribute labels; rather, it defines which clips are Deepfakes (synthetically manipulated) and which are not, and specifies method types used to create Deepfakes. The intended ML task is deepfake detection/classification of videos (with evaluation using metrics such as log loss and precision/weighted PR on real vs DFDC videos).
